styles.label: History
styles.blurb: Castle, Charles Bridge and the old Jewish quarter.

styles.label: Culture
styles.blurb: Museums, galleries, concerts and black-light theatre.

styles.label: Budget
styles.blurb: Cheap beer, trams and free views from the hills.

stays.why: Steps from Old Town Square and Charles Bridge. Walk to most sights; noisier at night.
Quiet cobbled lanes under the castle. Romantic and close to the bridge; fewer trams.
Leafy, local and full of cafés and restaurants. Good value; 15–20 minutes by tram or metro to the centre.
Central and practical around Wenceslas Square. Main train station and metro nearby; busy streets.

food: Try Czech classics: svíčková (beef in cream sauce), goulash with bread dumplings, and fried cheese.
Prague is famous for beer. A half-litre of local lager is often cheaper than a coffee; prices vary by pub.
Snack on a trdelník (chimney cake) from a street stall, or grab a chlebíček open sandwich from a deli.
Lunch menus (polední menu) at local pubs are the best value: a soup and main for a modest price.
Book popular dinner spots ahead for weekends. Many kitchens close early on Sunday.
more_time: Day trip to Kutná Hora: train from the main station, about an hour each way, to see the bone church and old town.
Swap one museum for a half-day at Vyšehrad: fortress walls, a cemetery of famous Czechs and river views.
Take a tram to Letná or Petřín for a park walk and a beer garden with a city view.

recommend.why: Three nights covers the castle, Old Town, the Jewish quarter and a day trip, without rushing.

month_notes: January: cold, highs around 4°C and lows near -2°C. Pack a warm coat; museums and pubs are cozy.
February: still cold, highs near 7°C. Fewer crowds; some sights keep shorter hours.
March: cool and changeable, highs around 10°C. Bring layers and a rain jacket.
April: mild, highs near 15°C. Good for walking; expect about 9 rain days.
May: pleasant, highs around 19°C. Busy and lively; book hotels early.
June: warm, highs near 25°C. Long evenings; around 12 rain days, so pack a light rain layer.
July: warmest month, highs around 26°C. Peak crowds; mornings are best for the bridge and castle.
August: hot and busy, highs near 26°C. Same advice: start early and rest midday.
September: mild and comfortable, highs around 21°C. Fewer rain days; a strong month to visit.
October: cooler, highs near 15°C. Golden autumn light; bring a jacket.
November: chilly, highs around 8°C. Grey skies and about 10 rain days; Christmas markets start late in the month.
December: cold, highs near 5°C. Christmas markets and festive lights; pack warm layers and waterproof shoes.

climate_guide.summary: Four clear seasons: cold winters, warm summers and mild spring and autumn. Rain is spread through the year.

items.title: Best time: May, June and September
items.text: Highs around 19–25°C with long days. Comfortable for walking the castle and old town.

items.title: Winter is cold (December to February)
items.text: Highs of 4–7°C and lows near or below freezing. Pack a warm coat, hat and gloves.

items.title: Rain all year
items.text: About 8–12 rain days every month. A small umbrella or rain jacket is always useful.

items.title: Cobblestones need good shoes
items.text: The old centre is paved with uneven stones. Wear comfortable, grippy shoes, especially when wet.

items.title: Summer is warm, not extreme
items.text: July and August peak near 26°C. Start sightseeing early and take a midday break.

items.title: What to pack
items.text: Layers for changeable days, a waterproof layer, walking shoes and a warm coat for winter.

transit.best: Walk the centre; use metro and trams for longer hops.

modes.text: Three lines (A, B, C) run roughly 05:00–24:00. Fast for crossing the city; not needed inside the old centre.
Trams cover the centre well. Buy tickets at yellow machines or in apps. A 90-minute ticket costs about 50 CZK; a 24-hour ticket about 150 CZK.
Buses mostly serve the outskirts and the airport. Use metro and trams for sightseeing.
Uber and Bolt work in Prague. Use them to avoid taxi touts.
Driving in the centre is slow and parking is restricted. Use P+R lots and take transit in.
The centre is walkable. Charles Bridge and Old Town are best on foot.
